evidence.claim: Pitfall, measured: if the server TRUNCATES float coordinates (int cast of a float column), the score drops -0.0040 overall. 6bba: -0.0047 (dTP -260, dFP +313). 44b6: +0.0002.

The public organiser converter reads float coordinates: csv_to_geffs.py casts z,y,x to pl.Float64 without rounding. The organisers' own geffs_to_csv.py writes integers: cast(Float64).round(0).cast(Int64).

The competition data description asks for node rows with 'node_id, t, z, y, x (integer centroid coordinates in voxels)'. Float output is therefore off-spec, and the server-side parser behaviour is unknown.

evidence.claim: GT node coordinates are int64 on the voxel grid, so GT carries its own quantisation. With a localisation error of ~1.8 um, far larger than the grid, removing the independent quantisation of our predictions helps in expectation. The empirical +0.0018 is the arbiter.
evidence.source: GT geff dtype check (notes); sample_submission.csv integer coords

evidence.claim: Earlier evidence pointed the other way: Friend B found rounding worth +0.0006 on 4 44b6 videos (2 of them leaky). That is within noise of our 199-video result, where 13 of 71 44b6 videos lose.
Eric's sub-voxel DETECTOR peak refinement lost -0.002 on LB twice. That was a different mechanism: it trusted in-sample detector features. This change only removes output quantisation.

implementation_notes: Mechanism confirmed. The metric matches every frame independently with optimal 1/(1+d) assignment within 7 um. It never rounds. Our int(round()) adds z quantisation noise (RMS ~0.44-0.47 um; mean |z frac| 0.22 voxel; 97.9% of output nodes are non-integer after linefit), which flips near-tie matches. Measured: +0.0018 adjusted edge J on 199 videos (dTP +70, dFP -190, dFN -70), same node count, division counts identical on all 87 GT-division videos. CONCRETE CODE: (1) exp48/x138-port notebook cell 7 write_test_submission, add a knob OUTPUT_FLOAT_COORDS = os.environ.get('BIOHUB_OUTPUT_FLOAT_COORDS','1')!='0' and write node z,y,x as f'{min(max(0.0, v), dim-1):.3f}' (dim = 64/256/256 from the frame shape) instead of max(0,int(round(v))). Format every node coordinate with a decimal point so that polars' schema inference (first 100 rows; node rows come first per dataset) sees Float64. Edge rows can keep -1. Keep t, node_id, source_id and target_id as ints. The upper clip is new and harmless (<0.5 voxel); floats above dim-1 could fail a range validator. (2) replay.write_geff: take a round_coords flag (default False to match the new writer) and skip round() when it is False; the GEFF already stores floats. Keep the old path for control replays so exp39 reproduces exactly. PITFALLS: (a) The spec says 'integer centroid coordinates' and the organisers' geffs_to_csv rounds, so the hosted parser may (i) cast Float64 (the gain lands), (ii) round (identical to today), (iii) truncate by an int cast of a float column (-0.004, measured; 6bba-like embryos are hurt, 44b6-like are neutral), or (iv) refuse to parse (scoring error, one probe lost). The public csv_to_geffs uses Float64, so (i) is most likely (guess). (b) Do not ship floats unrounded to many digits; 3 decimals is measured equal to full float (0.90427 vs 0.90422). (c) The win-rate gate fails literally because ~40-50% of videos are exact ties. Judge on the D-weighted delta and CI per embryo, or count wins among changed videos only (44b6 22/35 = 63%, 6bba 51/85 = 60%). (d) Transfer: on unseen test embryos the localisation error is larger, so quantisation is a smaller share of total error. Expect 60-90% transfer (guess). With the x138 head, localisation improves, so the rounding share, and the gain, should grow (guess, testable). (e) The linefit knobs already exist as env vars BIOHUB_OUTPUT_LINEFIT_WEIGHT (0.8) / BIOHUB_OUTPUT_LINEFIT_WINDOW (2) in notebook cell 2 and in build_probe_kernel. B28 tuned them with rounded output, so they must be re-tuned with floats. Linefit moves 354 GT-matched nodes beyond 7 um, so a displacement cap is a separate, compatible knob.
refined_change: Write node z,y,x as floats with 3 decimals, clipped to [0, dim-1], in write_test_submission, behind BIOHUB_OUTPUT_FLOAT_COORDS (default on). Keep all ints for t/ids/edge rows. Mirror the change in replay.write_geff with a round_coords flag. Topology and node count are unchanged. Stack it on exp48 (+ the edge filter / stitch if probes 29/30 hold, + the x138 head when ported). Then re-run the linefit grid with floats reaching the scorer.
refined_lab_test: CPU only, no GPU needed. Step 0 (already done on the exp39 tail): +0.0018 on 199 videos, divisions unchanged, floor -0.0040. Step 1: in the Kaggle CPU lab (tools/kaggle_lab.py), replay the current best tail (exp48 + edge filter) with write_geff round_coords=False against the same tail with rounding, scored by the official evaluate.py. SELECTION (64 6bba) then one CONFIRMATION (135). Success: >= +0.0015 on confirmation, each embryo > 0, identical node count, divJ unchanged. Use the changed-video win rate, because exact ties make the plain >=55% rule meaningless for an output-only change. Step 2: same lab, floats on, linefit grid BIOHUB_OUTPUT_LINEFIT_WEIGHT in {0.6, 0.8, 1.0} x BIOHUB_OUTPUT_LINEFIT_WINDOW in {2, 3} (6 cells). Pick on SELECTION and confirm once; adopt only if >= +0.0005 over (0.8, 2)-float and both embryos >= 0. Step 3: after the x138 head port, re-measure float vs round on its tail (expect a larger delta; guess). LB step: include floats in the next bundle only after a parse check. Best is one dedicated probe = best-known submission + floats only. The outcome tells us what the server does: equal to 3 decimals suggests the server rounds (harmless). Higher means Float64 (keep). A drop of >= 0.002 means truncation (revert immediately). A scoring error means integer-only parsing (revert; one probe lost).
expected_gain: Local +0.0018 measured (adjusted edge J; the division term measured unchanged), plus perhaps +0.0005..0.001 from a float-aware linefit retune (guess). Public +0.001..0.002 if the server keeps floats (guess: 60-90% transfer). 0 if it rounds, about -0.004 on a 6bba-like embryo if it truncates. That downside is detectable in one probe and reversible.
